C14 and C19 share some administration-specific conservation language and machinery, but neither matches the child as closely in addressee, purpose, and organization.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Dear Mr. Albright: I was gratified indeed to receive your letter and the assurance it contained about the merits of the conservation programs of this Administration.","parent_excerpt":"Dear Mr. Albright: I have been most interested to learn from time to time that your arrangements for a mid-century Conference on Resources have been taking shape","explanation":"Both are presidential letters directly to Albright that open by acknowledging his communication or conservation activity."},{"child_excerpt":"In every Department associated with the problems of soil and water, and of renewable resources, we have recommended programs","parent_excerpt":"the Government, as well as private groups—including industry, agriculture, labor, conservation, education—has a considerable responsibility for the better management of resources. Accordingly, I am asking the Secretary of Agriculture, the Secretary of the Interior, and other Federal officials concerned with resources","explanation":"Both frame conservation as a coordinated federal responsibility spanning departments and multiple classes of natural resources."},{"child_excerpt":"principles which ought not to be the basis of partisan politics","parent_excerpt":"undertake studies and promote discussion of national issues on a competent and nonpartisan basis","explanation":"The later letter closely adapts the earlier letter's explicit insistence that resource policy be treated nonpartisanly."},{"child_excerpt":"Your commendation ... is all the more reassuring in the light of your long and eminent leadership in a cause so important to the present and future generations of Americans.","parent_excerpt":"I hope the conservation movement ... will continue to prosper and grow in influence. This letter will assure you that you and your associates have my sincere wishes for a successful conference.","explanation":"Both conclude by affirming Albright's conservation work and its continuing national importance."}]}
